answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check and periodically renewed. The credential lets one real participant contribute once to a vote or reputation pool, so creating a nebula of accounts does not multiply their weight. An attacker must recruit and coordinate real people, pay for checks, and risk exposing the operation; a mirror of one person’s identity still earns only one credential, even at the zenith of account creation.
